arithmetic_class: degree-1 primitive L-function over Q (GL(1), trivial character); Tate motive Q(0)

critical_line.citation: Riemann (1859); Hardy (1914); Selberg (1942); Conrey (1989); de la Vallee Poussin (1896)
critical_line.detail: Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of zeta has Re s = 1/2. Open since 1859. Unconditional partial results: infinitely many zeros on the line (Hardy 1914); a positive proportion (Selberg 1942); more than two fifths (Conrey 1989); zero-free region Re s >= 1 - c/log|t| (de la Vallee Poussin 1896). Numerical verification of initial zeros exists but is not evidence used here.

definition: zeta(s) = sum_{n>=1} n^{-s} = prod_p (1 - p^{-s})^{-1} for Re s > 1, continued meromorphically to C. Local Satake datum at every prime p: A = [1], det(1 - A T) = 1 - T = [1, -1] (low-first), so a_{p^k} = 1 and a_n = 1 for all n.

L0_WELL_DEFINED.citation: Dirichlet series sum n^{-s} converges absolutely for Re s > 1; Euler (1737); B. Riemann (1859), 'Ueber die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Groesse'

L1_MULTIPLICATIVITY.citation: total multiplicativity of a_n == 1 is immediate; unique factorization: Euclid; Gauss (1801)
L1_MULTIPLICATIVITY.witness: a_n == 1 identically, hence a_{mn} = a_m a_n for all m,n (trivial complete proof); exact check for all m,n <= 60

L2_EULER_PRODUCT.citation: L. Euler (1737): zeta(s) = prod_p (1 - p^{-s})^{-1} for Re s > 1
L2_EULER_PRODUCT.witness: a_n = prod_p a_(p^v_p(n)) verified exactly for all n <= 200 from the degree-1 local data [1,-1]

L3_BOUNDED_DEGREE_RATIONAL.witness: every local factor has degree exactly 1: detector reconstructs P/Q = 1/(1 - T) (Berlekamp-Massey certified on 12 terms, held-out tail predicted exactly) at p = 2, 3, 5, 7; the same [1,-1] datum defines the local factor at every p by construction

L4_WEIGHT_DUALITY.citation: B. Riemann (1859), 'Ueber die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Groesse'
L4_WEIGHT_DUALITY.witness: op_dual_satake([1,-1], det=1) == [1,-1]: local data is exactly self-dual at every p (trivial character); inverse root a = 1 satisfies a^2 == p^0 exactly at p in {2,3,5,7}: local data pure of weight 0 (unitary normalization) — trivially, at EVERY p; consistent with the self-dual functional equation s <-> 1-s of weight-0 (Tate motive Q(0)) type

L5_CONDUCTOR_GAMMA_ROOT.citation: B. Riemann (1859), 'Ueber die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Groesse'
L5_CONDUCTOR_GAMMA_ROOT.witness: conductor N = 1, gamma factor pi^{-s/2} Gamma(s/2), root number +1: xi(s) = pi^{-s/2} Gamma(s/2) zeta(s) satisfies xi(s) = xi(1-s)

L6_CONTINUATION_FE.citation: B. Riemann (1859), 'Ueber die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Groesse'; J. Hadamard (1893), product factorization of xi
L6_CONTINUATION_FE.witness: zeta continues meromorphically to C with a single simple pole at s = 1 (residue 1) and functional equation xi(s) = xi(1-s); Hadamard product for xi

L7_TWIST_TENSOR_COMPAT.citation: P. G. L. Dirichlet (1837), L-functions of characters; functional equation of L(s,chi): Hurwitz (1882) / standard
L7_TWIST_TENSOR_COMPAT.witness: exact local tensor checks embedded in tensor_checks: zeta (x) zeta -> zeta locally, and zeta (x) chi_4 -> L(s, chi_4) locally at p = 3; globally, twisting zeta by any Dirichlet character chi gives L(s, chi), which has its own continuation and functional equation

L8_REALIZATION.citation: J. Tate (1950), doctoral thesis, Fourier analysis in number fields (published in Cassels-Froehlich 1967); B. Riemann (1859), 'Ueber die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Groesse'
L8_REALIZATION.witness: automorphic: zeta is the standard L-function of the trivial Hecke character on GL(1)/Q, with continuation and FE from adelic Poisson summation (Tate's thesis); motivic: L-function of the Tate motive Q(0) = H^0(Spec Q); classical: Mellin transform of the theta function (Riemann's second proof)

L9_EXPLICIT_FORMULA_POSITIVITY.citation: explicit formula: Riemann (1859), proved by H. von Mangoldt (1895); distributional form: A. P. Guinand (1948), A. Weil (1952); positivity criterion equivalent to RH: A. Weil (1952)
L9_EXPLICIT_FORMULA_POSITIVITY.witness: SPLIT: (i) the explicit formula itself is a THEOREM — sum over zeros of h(rho) = arch. terms - sum_p log p * (g(log p^k) + g(-log p^k))/p^{k/2} as a distribution identity; (ii) the POSITIVITY of the Weil functional W(g*g~) >= 0 on the relevant class is EQUIVALENT to RH (Weil's criterion) and is OPEN; no independent positivity input (no analogue of Frobenius weights / Castelnuovo positivity) is known for zeta

DUALITY_FE.citation: B. Riemann (1859), 'Ueber die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Groesse'
DUALITY_FE.witness: supplied by theta inversion / Poisson summation; self-dual: op_dual_satake([1,-1], det=1) == [1,-1]: local data is exactly self-dual at every p (trivial character)

EULER_PRODUCT.witness: supplied by unique factorization in Z; local factors degree 1; a_n = prod_p a_(p^v_p(n)) verified exactly for all n <= 200 from the degree-1 local data [1,-1]

FAMILY.citation: P. G. L. Dirichlet (1837); functional equations: Hurwitz (1882), Hecke (1917) for zeta_K
FAMILY.witness: zeta is the q = 1 member of the family of Dirichlet L-functions {L(s, chi)}, each with Euler product, continuation and functional equation; it is also the Dedekind zeta of Q inside {zeta_K}

POSITIVITY_PURITY.citation: function-field contrast: A. Weil (1948), P. Deligne (1974)
POSITIVITY_PURITY.witness: local purity of weight 0 holds trivially and exactly (inverse root a = 1 satisfies a^2 == p^0 exactly at p in {2,3,5,7}: local data pure of weight 0 (unitary normalization) — trivially, at EVERY p), but this is vacuous for the global question; no independently defined positivity mechanism known — this is precisely the missing structure (#763). In the function-field analogue this slot is filled by Frobenius weights via the Castelnuovo/Hodge-index positivity (Weil 1948, Deligne 1974); no analogue over Q is known

TENSOR_OPS.witness: degree-1 objects: tensor operations are trivially closed; exact checks zeta (x) zeta and zeta (x) chi_4 at p = 3 embedded in tensor_checks (A6 HOLDS in both); twists land in the Dirichlet L family

TRACE_FORMULA.witness: the Riemann-von Mangoldt / Guinand-Weil explicit formula is an unconditional distribution identity pairing zeros against prime powers — a genuine 'trace formula' shape; what it is the trace OF (a self-adjoint operator) is not known — see POSITIVITY_PURITY

notes: The single degree of structural freedom this world is missing is the POSITIVITY_PURITY mechanism: every other row of the matrix is filled by a classical theorem, and L9 fails to close only because Weil positivity is RH-equivalent rather than independently supplied.
